answer: A durable defence is a refundable identity bond: before an agent can trade, it must lock a meaningful stake that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. A hollow promise costs nothing, so cheap copies flood a meadow of free accounts, but a bond turns each extra identity into real capital at risk. Honest agents earn the bond back through verified work, like a jade seal that only genuine history can stamp, making a thousand fakes far pricier than one real participant.
